C.description: Rotary axis around Z. On lathes the spindle angle for driven tools.
C.label: C axis

D.description: Number of the cutter radius offset that G41 and G42 apply.
D.label: Radius offset register

F.description: Feed rate. The unit follows the feed mode: distance per minute with G94, per spindle revolution with G95. In a threading block it is the thread lead.
F.label: Feed

G.description: Tells the control how to read the block: motion type, plane, units, offsets and cycles.
G.label: Preparatory function

H.description: Number of the tool length offset that G43 applies. CAM output usually writes the tool number here.
H.label: Length offset register

I.description: Distance from the arc start point to the arc centre along X, used with G2 and G3 in the XY and ZX planes.
I.label: Arc centre along X

J.description: Distance from the arc start point to the arc centre along Y, used with G2 and G3 in the XY and YZ planes.
J.label: Arc centre along Y

K.description: Distance from the arc start point to the arc centre along Z in the ZX and YZ planes. In a drilling cycle it is the number of repeats.
K.label: Arc centre along Z, or repeat count

L.description: How many times a cycle or a call is repeated.
L.label: Repeat count

M.description: Switches a machine function such as spindle, coolant or the tool change. Apart from the common ones such as M19, M29, M30, M98 and M99, numbers above M9 are set by the machine builder.
M.label: Miscellaneous function

N.description: Names the block so that jumps and cycles can point at it. It has no effect on the motion.
N.label: Block number

O.description: Number of a program or subprogram, written in the first block of it.
O.label: Program number

P.description: Dwell time in milliseconds with G4, the program number with M98, or the block number a code refers back to.
P.label: Program number, dwell or block reference

Q.description: Peck depth in a drilling cycle, the shift amount in a boring cycle, or a block number in a lathe multi-pass cycle.
Q.label: Peck depth or shift

R.description: Arc radius with G2 and G3, the retract plane of a drilling cycle, or a retract amount in a lathe cycle.
R.label: Radius or retract plane

S.description: Spindle speed in revolutions per minute, or the surface speed while G96 is active.
S.label: Spindle speed

T.description: Tool number. On lathes the digits also carry the offset register, so T0101 is station 1 with offset 1.
T.label: Tool

U.description: Extra linear axis on mills. On lathes an incremental X move (as a diameter), a cycle allowance, or a dwell time with G4.
U.label: U axis

V.description: Extra linear axis on mills. On lathes an incremental Y move.
V.label: V axis

W.description: Extra linear axis on mills. On lathes an incremental Z move or a cycle allowance.
W.label: W axis

X.description: Target position on the X axis. On lathes X is a diameter. With G4 it is a dwell time in seconds.
X.label: X axis

Y.description: Target position on the Y axis.
Y.label: Y axis

Z.description: Target position on the Z axis.
Z.label: Z axis

codes.description: Moves to the target at rapid speed. The axes are not interpolated, so the path can bend.
codes.label: Rapid positioning

codes.description: Straight move to the target at the active feed.
codes.label: Linear feed move

codes.description: Arc to the target in the active plane, turning clockwise. The centre comes from I, J and K measured from the arc start, or from a radius R.
codes.label: Circular move, clockwise

codes.description: Arc to the target in the active plane, turning counter-clockwise. The centre comes from I, J and K measured from the arc start, or from a radius R.
codes.label: Circular move, counter-clockwise

codes.description: Holds the tool where it is before the next block runs. It applies to this block only.
codes.label: Dwell

codes.description: Switches the look-ahead contour control for fast, accurate machining of many short blocks on with P10000 and off again with P0. Write it in a block of its own.
codes.label: AI contour control, on and off

codes.description: Q chooses a high-speed mode: 1 contour control with look-ahead, 2 smoothing interpolation, 3 nano smoothing, 0 ends the mode. Write it in a block of its own. Axis words in the block, such as X0 Y0 Z0, only name the axes the mode applies to; nothing moves.
codes.label: Contour control and smoothing modes

codes.description: Wraps the path of a rotary axis around a cylinder, so that a contour on the unrolled surface can be written as a flat one. The rotary axis word carries the cylinder radius to start the mode and 0 to end it, each in a block of its own. The positions in between are on the unrolled surface, not in the coordinates of the rest of the program.
codes.label: Cylindrical interpolation

codes.description: The tool slows down to a stop at the end of this block before the next one starts. It applies to this block only; G61 does the same for every block.
codes.label: Exact stop for this block

codes.description: Writes a tool offset, a work coordinate system or a parameter from the program: L says which table, P which entry. The other words of the block are the values written there, not a move, a feed or a speed.
codes.label: Data setting

codes.description: Turns moves programmed on a flat plane, made of one linear and one rotary axis, into moves of those two axes, so that the rotary axis can mill a flat face. Write it in a block of its own; G13.1 ends it. Axis words of the block, such as X and C, give the centre of the rotary axis on that plane. In between, the positions are on the plane, not in the coordinates of the rest of the program.
codes.label: Polar coordinate interpolation on

codes.description: Ends the polar coordinate interpolation that G12.1 started and gives back the plane that was selected before it.
codes.label: Polar coordinate interpolation off

codes.description: Ends the polar coordinate command of G16: the axis words of the plane are coordinates again.
codes.label: Polar coordinate command off

codes.description: From here on, until G15, the end point of a move is given in polar form in the selected plane: the word of the first axis of the plane is the radius, the word of the second the angle, counter-clockwise from the first axis. Under G90 the radius is measured from the zero point of the work coordinate system (of a G52 local system, where one is set), under G91 from the current position.
codes.label: Polar coordinate command

codes.description: Selects XY as the working plane. Arcs use I and J, and a drilling cycle feeds along Z.
codes.label: XY plane

codes.description: Selects ZX as the working plane. Arcs use I and K, and a drilling cycle feeds along Y.
codes.label: ZX plane

codes.description: Selects YZ as the working plane. Arcs use J and K, and a drilling cycle feeds along X.
codes.label: YZ plane

codes.description: Dimensions in the program are read as inches. Set it before the first dimension word.
codes.label: Inch input

codes.description: Dimensions in the program are read as millimetres. Set it before the first dimension word.
codes.label: Millimetre input

codes.description: Moves at rapid, first to the intermediate point written in the block (in the program's coordinates, absolute or incremental), then to the machine reference point.
codes.label: Return to the reference point

params.label: Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to the reference point, in the program's coordinates

codes.description: Moves at rapid to a further reference point, often the tool change position, by way of the intermediate point written in the block (in the program's coordinates, absolute or incremental). P says which point; without it the second is meant.
codes.label: Return to the second, third or fourth reference point

params.label: Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates
Intermediate point on the way to that reference point, in the program's coordinates

codes.description: One straight threading pass on a lathe in G-code system A. F carries the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate, so scaling the feed would change the thread.
codes.label: Thread cutting pass

codes.description: One straight threading pass; this is how G-code systems B and C spell G32. F carries the thread lead per revolution, not a feed rate.
codes.label: Thread cutting pass

codes.description: Cuts a thread whose lead grows or shrinks by K with every spindle revolution. F is the lead at the start point, not a feed rate, so scaling the feed would change the thread.
codes.label: Thread cutting with a variable lead

params.label: Change of the lead per spindle revolution

codes.description: Turns radius compensation off. Do it during a retract move, not in an arc.
codes.label: Cancel cutter radius compensation

codes.description: Offsets the path by the tool radius to the left of the direction of travel. Mills take the radius from the register D, lathes from the tool offset. Switch it on during an approach move.
codes.label: Cutter radius compensation, left

codes.description: Offsets the path by the tool radius to the right of the direction of travel. Mills take the radius from the register D, lathes from the tool offset. Switch it on during an approach move.
codes.label: Cutter radius compensation, right

codes.description: Applies the tool length from the offset register named by H while moving in the tool axis.
codes.label: Tool length offset

params.label: Target position in the tool axis

codes.description: Keeps the tool tip on the programmed path while the rotary axes move; the block writes the end positions of the rotary axes and the length offset register H. The move of this block itself only applies the length offset, and the control starts after it. G49 ends it.
codes.label: Tool centre point control, by rotary positions

codes.description: Keeps the tool tip on the programmed path while the tool tilts; the block writes the direction of the tool axis as I, J and K instead of rotary positions, and the length offset register H. The move of this block itself only applies the length offset, and the control starts after it. G49 ends it.
codes.label: Tool centre point control, by tool direction

params.label: Tilt of the tool in the direction of travel

codes.description: Applies the tool length from the offset register named by H the other way round than G43. CAM output normally writes G43.
codes.label: Tool length offset, negative

params.label: Target position in the tool axis

codes.description: Drops the active tool length offset. It also ends tool centre point control (G43.4, G43.5). It is part of the usual safe-start block.
codes.label: Cancel tool length offset

codes.description: Ends scaling on a machining centre; G51 switches it on. gEdit still reads an S word in such a block as a spindle-speed clamp, because a lathe program in G-code system A writes its clamp as G50 S and may be opened with this profile by mistake.
codes.label: Scaling cancel

codes.description: Ends the mirror image of G51.1 for the axes named in the block. The values of the axis words are not used.
codes.label: Programmable mirror image off

codes.description: Enlarges or reduces the programmed shape. The axis words give the centre of the scaling, P the factor for all axes or I, J and K a factor per axis; G50 ends it. Positions written after it are not the positions the tool reaches.
codes.label: Scaling

codes.description: Mirrors the following moves about the position the axis words give; the words are the place of the mirror axis, not a move. G50.1 ends it. Positions written after it are not the positions the tool reaches.
codes.label: Programmable mirror image

codes.description: Sets a local coordinate system inside the active work offset. The axis words give where its zero lies, so they are a shift and not a move; G52 with every axis at zero ends it.
codes.label: Local coordinate system

codes.description: Reads the positions of this block in machine coordinates instead of the work offset. It needs absolute values and is often used to move to a tool change position.
codes.label: Machine coordinates for this block

codes.description: Write it alone in the block after G68.2 or G68.4: the rotary axes move so that the tool stands at right angles to the tilted plane.
codes.label: Turn the tool axis to the tilted plane

codes.description: Selects the first work coordinate system.
codes.label: Work offset 1

codes.description: Selects the second work coordinate system.
codes.label: Work offset 2

codes.description: Selects the third work coordinate system.
codes.label: Work offset 3

codes.description: Selects the fourth work coordinate system.
codes.label: Work offset 4

codes.description: Selects the fifth work coordinate system.
codes.label: Work offset 5

codes.description: Selects the sixth work coordinate system.
codes.label: Work offset 6

codes.description: Selects one of the additional work coordinate systems. P names which one.
codes.label: Extended work offset

codes.description: The tool slows down to a stop at the end of every cutting block before the next one starts. In force until G62, G63 or G64.
codes.label: Exact stop mode

codes.description: Lowers the feed at inside corners while the cutter radius compensation is on. In force until G61, G63 or G64.
codes.label: Automatic corner override

codes.description: Tapping with a compensating chuck: the feed override and the feed hold have no effect and the tool does not slow down at the end of a block. The feed is the spindle speed times the pitch, so neither may be scaled on its own. In force until G61, G62 or G64.
codes.label: Tapping mode

codes.description: The normal mode: the next block starts without the tool stopping at the end of the last one. Ends G61, G62 and G63.
codes.label: Cutting mode

codes.description: Runs the macro program P once. The other words of the block are its arguments, handed over as local variables, not moves, feeds or speeds of this program.
codes.label: Macro call

codes.description: Runs the macro program P after every following move until G67. The other words of this block are its arguments, not moves, feeds or speeds of this program.
codes.label: Modal macro call

codes.description: Runs the macro program P after every following block, not only after moves, until G67. The other words of this block are its arguments, not moves, feeds or speeds of this program.
codes.label: Modal macro call in every block

codes.description: Ends the modal macro call of G66.
codes.label: Modal macro call off

codes.description: Turns the coordinate system. In the selected plane the axis words give the centre of the rotation and R the angle; with I, J and K it is a three-dimensional rotation about that direction. G69 ends it. On a lathe with two turrets the same number is a mirror image instead.
codes.label: Coordinate system rotation

codes.description: Defines a coordinate system tilted against the workpiece and makes it the one the program is written in. X, Y and Z give its origin; I, J and K give the three Euler angles, or with P another way to define the plane (P1 roll-pitch-yaw angles with Q as the order of the turns, P2 three points, P3 two vectors, P4 projection angles). G69 ends it. G53.1 in the next block turns the rotary axes to the new tool direction.
codes.label: Tilted working plane

params.label: How the plane is defined: none Euler angles, 1 to 4 another form
Order of the turns (P1) or the number of the point or vector (P2, P3)
First angle, or X component of a vector
Second angle, or Y component of a vector
Third angle, or Z component of a vector
Turn about the new Z axis (P2)

codes.description: Makes the coordinate system whose Z axis is the present direction of the tool the one the program is written in. X, Y and Z give its origin in absolute values (the present position when left out); R turns it about its Z axis. G69 ends it.
codes.label: Tilted working plane from the tool direction

params.label: Turn about the new Z axis

codes.description: Tilts again, relative to the tilted plane that is in force. It is written like G68.2 (P chooses the form), and its origin is given in the coordinates of that plane. Tool length and radius compensation must be off. G69 ends it.
codes.label: Tilted working plane, added to the one in force

params.label: How the plane is defined: none Euler angles, 1 to 4 another form
Order of the turns (P1) or the number of the point or vector (P2, P3)
First angle, or X component of a vector
Second angle, or Y component of a vector
Third angle, or Z component of a vector
Turn about the new Z axis (P2)

codes.description: Ends G68, G68.2, G68.3 and G68.4 and goes back to the coordinates of the program. On a lathe with two turrets the same number ends the mirror image instead.
codes.label: Coordinate system rotation off

codes.description: The way a lathe control writes the end of a tilted plane or a three-dimensional rotation; a machining centre writes G69.
codes.label: Tilted working plane off, lathe spelling

codes.description: Drills in steps of Q and pulls back only a short way between the steps to break the chip. On lathes in G-code system A, G73 repeats a profile for a pre-shaped blank instead.
codes.label: Peck drilling cycle with chip break

codes.description: Cuts a left-hand thread: the spindle turns back at the bottom of the hole. F carries the pitch, so scaling the feed would change the thread. On lathes in G-code system A, G74 is a face pecking or grooving cycle instead.
codes.label: Left-hand tapping cycle

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Bores to depth, turns the spindle to a fixed angle and shifts the tool by Q clear of the wall before retracting. On lathes in G-code system A, G76 is a multi-pass threading cycle whose F is the thread lead.
codes.label: Fine boring cycle

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Ends the active drilling or boring cycle. Any code from the motion group cancels it as well.
codes.label: Cancel the canned cycle

codes.description: Feeds down to Z and pulls out at rapid. Every following block that carries a position drills another hole, until G80.
codes.label: Drilling cycle

codes.description: Like G81, but waits at the hole bottom for the time given by P before pulling out. The dwell cleans up the bottom of a flat hole.
codes.label: Drilling cycle with dwell

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Drills in steps of Q and pulls all the way back to the retract plane after each step, so the chips clear. Active until G80.
codes.label: Peck drilling cycle

codes.description: Cuts a right-hand thread: the spindle turns back at the bottom of the hole. F carries the pitch (pitch times speed with G94, pitch with G95), so scaling the feed would change the thread. Rigid tapping is normally switched on with an M code in the block before.
codes.label: Tapping cycle

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Rigid tapping of a right-hand thread, written in the block format of an older control generation. F carries the pitch, so scaling the feed would change the thread.
codes.label: Rigid tapping cycle, older block format

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Rigid tapping of a left-hand thread, written in the block format of an older control generation. F carries the pitch, so scaling the feed would change the thread.
codes.label: Left-hand rigid tapping cycle, older block format

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Feeds down to Z and feeds back out again, which leaves a cleaner wall than a rapid retract.
codes.label: Boring cycle

codes.description: Feeds down to Z, stops the spindle and pulls out at rapid.
codes.label: Boring cycle with spindle stop

codes.description: Bores a face on the underside of the workpiece, shifting by Q to get the tool through the hole. On lathes in G-code system A, G87 drills into the side of the part along X instead.
codes.label: Back boring cycle

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Feeds down to Z, dwells and stops so that the operator pulls the tool out by hand. It is rare in CAM output. On lathes in G-code system A, G88 taps along X instead.
codes.label: Boring cycle with manual retract

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Feeds down to Z, waits for the time given by P and feeds back out.
codes.label: Boring cycle with dwell

params.label: Dwell at the bottom in milliseconds

codes.description: Position words are read as coordinates in the active work offset. On lathes in G-code system A, G90 is a turning cycle instead and incremental moves use U and W.
codes.label: Absolute positions

codes.description: Position words are read as distances from the current position. G-code system A on lathes has no G91.
codes.label: Incremental positions

codes.description: Sets the work coordinate system, or with an S word clamps the top spindle speed; lathes in G-code system B and C use the number the same way. In system A this number is the single-pass threading cycle instead, so gEdit never scales the F of such a block.
codes.label: Coordinate set, spindle speed clamp

codes.description: The F word no longer gives a speed but the reciprocal of the time the block may take, so F12.5 runs the block in 4.8 seconds. Every move needs its own F while this mode is on.
codes.label: Inverse time feed

params.label: One divided by the block time in minutes

codes.description: F is read as distance per minute. On lathes in G-code system A, G94 is a facing cycle and the feed modes are G98 and G99 instead.
codes.label: Feed per minute

codes.description: F is read as distance per spindle revolution, which keeps the chip thickness steady when the speed changes.
codes.label: Feed per revolution

codes.description: S is read as surface speed, and the control raises the spindle speed as the diameter gets smaller. Clamp the top speed in a block of its own beforehand.
codes.label: Constant surface speed

codes.description: S is read as revolutions per minute again and the speed stays where it is set.
codes.label: Fixed spindle speed

codes.description: After each hole the cycle pulls back to the level the tool was at when the cycle started, which clears clamps between holes. On lathes in G-code system A, G98 means feed per minute instead.
codes.label: Cycle return to the initial level

codes.description: After each hole the cycle pulls back only to the R plane, which is quicker. On lathes in G-code system A, G99 means feed per revolution instead.
codes.label: Cycle return to the retract plane

codes.description: Stops the program where it is. The operator restarts it with cycle start.
codes.label: Program stop

codes.description: Stops the program only while the operator has the optional-stop switch on. Posts write it between operations for a check.
codes.label: Optional stop

codes.description: Ends the program without winding back to the start.
codes.label: Program end

codes.description: Starts the spindle clockwise at the active S speed.
codes.label: Spindle on, clockwise

codes.description: Starts the spindle counter-clockwise at the active S speed.
codes.label: Spindle on, counter-clockwise

codes.description: Stops the spindle.
codes.label: Spindle stop

codes.description: Changes to the tool that T selects. Turret lathes change on the T word alone and do not use M6.
codes.label: Tool change

codes.description: Turns on the second coolant supply. Whether that is mist, air or through the tool depends on the machine.
codes.label: Second coolant on

codes.description: Turns the flood coolant on.
codes.label: Coolant on

codes.description: Turns the coolant off.
codes.label: Coolant off

codes.description: Turns the spindle to a fixed angle and holds it there, for instance before a boring tool is pulled out. The angle is machine specific.
codes.label: Spindle orientation

codes.description: Announces rigid tapping for the tapping cycle in the next block, so the control drives the spindle and the feed in step instead of relying on a compensating chuck. Which M number does this is set by a machine parameter and can differ on your machine.
codes.label: Rigid tapping on

codes.description: Ends the program and returns to its start, ready for the next part.
codes.label: Program end and rewind

codes.description: Runs the subprogram whose number P gives and continues after it returns. Digits in front of the last four of P repeat the call.
codes.label: Subprogram call

codes.description: Ends a subprogram and returns to the caller. With P it returns to that block number instead of the block after the call. In a main program M99 starts the program over.
codes.label: Subprogram end

codes.description: Runs the program whose number P gives from an external device or a data server and continues after it returns.
codes.label: External subprogram call

codes.description: Reads the condition in brackets behind it and, when the condition holds, jumps with GOTO or runs the statement behind THEN. Otherwise the block does nothing.
codes.label: Conditional branch

codes.description: Continues at the block with this N number. The target has to exist in the same program.
codes.label: Jump to a block

codes.description: Introduces the statement an IF runs when its condition holds, usually an assignment.
codes.label: Statement of an IF

codes.description: Repeats the blocks up to the matching END as long as the condition in brackets holds. The number behind DO and END pairs the two.
codes.label: Loop head

codes.description: Opens the body of a WHILE loop. Its number has to match the END that closes the body.
codes.label: Loop body start

codes.description: Closes the body of the WHILE loop with the same number.
codes.label: Loop body end

codes.description: Comparison inside a condition: true when both sides have the same value.
codes.label: Equal to

codes.description: Comparison inside a condition: true when the two sides differ.
codes.label: Not equal to

codes.description: Comparison inside a condition: true when the left side is larger than the right one.
codes.label: Greater than

codes.description: Comparison inside a condition: true when the left side is smaller than the right one.
codes.label: Less than

codes.description: Comparison inside a condition: true when the left side is larger than the right one or the same.
codes.label: Greater than or equal

codes.description: Comparison inside a condition: true when the left side is smaller than the right one or the same.
codes.label: Less than or equal

codes.description: Joins two conditions: true only when both of them hold.
codes.label: Logical and

codes.description: Joins two conditions: true when at least one of them holds.
codes.label: Logical or

codes.description: Joins two conditions: true when exactly one of them holds.
codes.label: Logical exclusive or

codes.description: Gives what is left over after dividing the left side by the right one.
codes.label: Remainder

codes.description: Sine of the angle in the brackets. Angles are written in degrees, with the minutes as a decimal part: 90 degrees 30 minutes is 90.5.
codes.label: Sine

codes.description: Cosine of the angle in the brackets, in degrees.
codes.label: Cosine

codes.description: Tangent of the angle in the brackets, in degrees.
codes.label: Tangent

codes.description: Gives the angle, in degrees, whose sine is the value in the brackets. The value has to lie between -1 and 1, or the control raises an alarm. A control parameter chooses whether the result runs from 270 to 90 degrees or from -90 to 90 degrees.
codes.label: Arc sine

codes.description: Gives the angle, in degrees, whose cosine is the value in the brackets, from 180 down to 0. The value has to lie between -1 and 1, or the control raises an alarm.
codes.label: Arc cosine

codes.description: With one value in the brackets it gives the principal angle, from -90 to 90 degrees. With two values, written ATAN[#j]/[#k] or ATAN[#j,#k], it gives the direction in degrees of the point (#k, #j) in the X-Y plane, from 0 to 360 or, by a control parameter, from -180 to 180. In a division, put the one-value form in its own brackets or it is read as the two-value form.
codes.label: Arc tangent

codes.description: The short spelling of ATAN, with the same two forms and the same result.
codes.label: Arc tangent (short form)

codes.description: Square root of the value in the brackets.
codes.label: Square root

codes.description: The short spelling of SQRT.
codes.label: Square root (short form)

codes.description: Gives the value in the brackets without its sign.
codes.label: Absolute value

codes.description: Converts the value in the brackets from BCD to a binary number. Typically used on signal values exchanged with the machine.
codes.label: Convert BCD to binary

codes.description: Converts the value in the brackets from a binary number to BCD. Typically used on signal values exchanged with the machine.
codes.label: Convert binary to BCD

codes.description: Rounds to a whole number when it stands in a calculation or in an IF or WHILE condition: 1.2345 gives 1.0. Written at an address of an NC word, it rounds to the smallest input increment of that address instead.
codes.label: Round

codes.description: The short spelling of ROUND.
codes.label: Round (short form)

codes.description: Drops the decimals: 1.2 gives 1.0 and -1.2 gives -1.0, so the value moves towards zero.
codes.label: Round down to a whole number

codes.description: Rounds away from zero to the next whole number: 1.2 gives 2.0 and -1.2 gives -2.0.
codes.label: Round up to a whole number

codes.description: Natural logarithm of the value in the brackets. A value of zero or less raises an alarm.
codes.label: Natural logarithm

codes.description: The number e raised to the power of the value in the brackets. A result too large for the control raises an alarm.
codes.label: Exponential

codes.description: Raises the first value in the brackets to the power of the second: POW[#j,#k] is #j to the power of #k.
codes.label: Power

codes.description: Inside a macro, ADP[#n] gives an argument that was passed without a decimal point the point it would have had if it had been written with one, so the increment system does not change its value. Writing the point in the macro call is the more portable way.
codes.label: Add a decimal point

codes.description: Addresses an axis by its number instead of its name: AX[1]=100.0 gives the first axis the value 100. It is always followed by an equals sign. The number may be a variable or an expression, written in brackets.
codes.label: Indirect axis address

codes.description: Gives the number of the axis with the name in the brackets, for example #500=AXNUM[X]. An axis name the machine does not have raises an alarm.
codes.label: Axis number

codes.description: Opens the connection to the external input and output device. It stands before the first BPRNT or DPRNT.
codes.label: Open the data output

codes.description: Closes the connection to the external input and output device. It stands after the last BPRNT or DPRNT.
codes.label: Close the data output

codes.description: Sends characters and variable values to the external device as readable text. A variable is written as #number followed, in brackets, by the digits before and after the decimal point. Leading zeros become spaces or are left out, by a control setting. It stands between POPEN and PCLOS.
codes.label: Print as text

codes.description: Sends characters and variable values to the external device as binary numbers, each variable with the number of decimals given in brackets behind it. It stands between POPEN and PCLOS.
codes.label: Print as binary
